findings.claim: A missing `)` in an if condition is reported on the wrong line. With `if (input.equals("quit") {` on line 3, the editor shows "Error, line 12: ')' expected. Every ( needs a matching ): check the brackets on line 12." Line 12 is `return "unknown";`, and its brackets are balanced. By 14.9 the header is `if ( Expression ) Statement`, so the `)` is missing before the `{` on line 3, and that is the line to change. A single-line case (a missing `)` inside one return statement) is reported on its own line, so only the header-plus-block shape is affected. Rated medium: a missing `)` before `{` is a common beginner slip, the message sends the learner to a line that is already correct, and the line reported is part of simulator fidelity. Reproduced headless in Chromium (Playwright) against the current bytes at c0066ed8; no JDK is installed, so javac was not run and its exact wording is not asserted.
findings.recommendation: When the statement pass meets an unclosed `(` in an if, for or while header and then reaches the `{` that opens its body (or a depth-0 `;`), report "')' expected" at after() of the token before that `{`/`;`, so the line shown is the header line. Never report it at the end of the enclosing body.
